$comment: Cross-SDK conformance vectors for mapping the OpenAI Responses API's server-sent events onto IndeRun's canonical provider stream events. The Web, Swift, and Kotlin OpenAI adapters each implement this mapping separately, so they are held to one set of vectors rather than three hand-written suites that could drift. 'sse' is the raw response body as the streaming HTTP host capability would deliver it; 'expected' is the provider-shaped event sequence the adapter must produce, which the engine then normalizes into canonical StreamEvents. An expected entry of kind 'error' names the mapped IndeRun error class and message rather than a provider payload, since that mapping is the point of the case; when it also names 'retryable', the mapped error must carry that value. Cases prefixed 'openrouter_' encode the Responses dialect OpenRouter documents; they are derived from its published reference, not recorded from a live account.

cases.name: deltas_then_completed
cases.description: The common path: text deltas, then a completed response carrying the final text and usage.

cases.name: incomplete_maps_to_length
cases.description: A run truncated by max_output_tokens completes with finishReason 'length', matching what Mode 1 reports for the same response.

cases.name: unknown_event_types_are_ignored
cases.description: The Responses event set is open and additive, so unrecognized types must not fail the run.

cases.name: output_array_shape_is_walked
cases.description: A completed response that carries its text in the output array rather than output_text resolves the same way.

cases.name: rate_limit_error_event
cases.description: Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints nest the failure under an error object on the error event; both shapes are accepted.

cases.name: root_level_error_event
cases.description: The standalone `error` event carries code and message at its root, not nested under an error object. This is the shape the OpenAI Responses streaming reference documents.
cases.sse:
event: error
data: {"type": "error", "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "Rate limit reached for gpt-5.2", "param": null, "sequence_number": 1}

cases.name: response_failed_event
cases.description: response.failed carries its error nested under the response object.

expected.message: The model failed to generate a response.

cases.name: openrouter_keepalive_comments_and_routed_model
cases.description: OpenRouter interleaves SSE comment lines as keep-alives and echoes the routed vendor/model id on the completed response.

cases.name: openrouter_response_error_event
cases.description: A mid-stream failure arrives as a response.error event, which ends the stream like error does.

cases.name: openrouter_numeric_error_code_rate_limit
cases.description: OpenRouter's error code is the HTTP status as a number. 429 maps to RateLimited exactly as the HTTP status would.

cases.name: openrouter_numeric_error_code_insufficient_credits
cases.description: Code 402 (insufficient credits) makes the target unusable until the account is topped up, so it is Unavailable and not retryable.

cases.name: openrouter_numeric_error_code_auth
cases.sse:
event: error
data: {"type":"error","error":{"code":401,"message":"No auth credentials found"}}

cases.name: openrouter_untyped_mid_stream_error
cases.description: OpenRouter documents mid-stream failures as an event with a top-level error object (numeric code, metadata) and no event type. The HTTP status is already 200, so the event alone ends the run.

cases.name: openrouter_response_failed_typed_authentication
cases.description: OpenRouter collapses many causes into the native code server_error and keeps the precise classification in error_type on the response object. A typed 'authentication' failure is an AuthError, not a transient Unavailable.

cases.name: openrouter_response_failed_typed_timeout
cases.description: A typed 'timeout' failure is a retryable Timeout.

cases.name: openrouter_untyped_error_typed_rate_limit
cases.description: On an untyped error event the typed classification is in error.metadata.error_type and wins over the numeric code.
